column2: req_desc

Run manifest and health check
Ship `/app/run.json` with install, build and serve commands and answer `GET /api/health` on the published port as Deployment specifies.

District seeded on start
On start the app creates its schema and the seed district from Seed data when the database is empty, and leaves existing records untouched otherwise.

Sign-in and role landing
Seeded people sign in with email and password and land on their role's home route, every page except sign-in requires a session, and a return path is honoured only as Feedback states qualifies.

One error shape and precedence
Every API error uses the error shapes and the single precedence order stated in API.

Server boundary
The server serves only the app and its API on one origin, refuses oversized or wrongly typed bodies, and never serves source files or credentials, as qualified in Server boundary.

Service settings from the environment
Every service address and credential is read from the environment variables in Configuration and secrets and never appears in source or in anything sent to the browser.

Starts with a service down
With the object store or the mail service unreachable the app starts, answers its health check and serves every screen, and work that needs the missing service waits as Services describes.

Published viewports and tap targets
Every screen renders at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 with no horizontal scrolling, and every control in the public controls table presents a hit area at least 44 by 44 pixels at each of them.

Operational desk look
Every signed-in screen leads with the live megalitre counter Screens and layout names for it, on a warm paper ground with near-black ink and decimal-aligned tabular numerals, and the single cobalt accent appears only on the next irreversible action.

Purposeful motion only
Only the motions named in Motion and effects run, nothing loops for decoration, and under reduced motion each sequence shows its end state at once except the dwell timing itself.

Server-quoted order form
The grower's order form shows turnout, window, the server's window status, volume, nominated operators, and the flow rate, window remaining and any volume error from the server's quote for the latest input only, as laid out in Public screens and controls and Interactions.

Place an order
`POST /api/orders` schedules an order that fits, debiting the window's remaining volume and the grower's allocation in one step, and answers 201 with the order.

Ordering horizon
Orders open 10 days before a window opens and close at its closing instant, judged by the server, with the rejections in API.

Server-judged window status
Each window's status and orderability come from the server, and every open screen that shows them, including the window status on each gate card, changes within 5 seconds of each server status instant without a reload, even when the device clock is frozen or hours wrong.

One conversion rule
Window cap volumes, including pro-rated restricted ones, turnout max volumes and order flow rates are converted once on the server by the rule in Business rules, and every surface shows those exact values.

Allocation and turnout guards
An order beyond the grower's remaining allocation, on a busy turnout, or naming an unusable operator is refused with the statuses in API and changes nothing.

Grower ordering journey
A grower signs in, fills the order form, places the order and lands on `/orders/<order number>` showing it scheduled with their allocation reduced, and reloading that address shows the same order.

One winner for contested volume
Orders arriving at the same instant are judged against the window and the grower's allocation together, so exactly one takes the last window volume or the last allocation and the rest answer 409 `window_full` or 422 on `volume_ml` as Business rules sets, with nothing counted twice.

Capacity taken dialog
A grower whose order loses on capacity sees the Capacity taken dialog with its published copy, with focus held inside it until it closes and then returned to the Place order button.

Conflict notice to the losing grower
Every order refused with `window_full` sends the losing grower one conflict notice email carrying their own unchanged allocation as described in Services, and an order refused on allocation or on the turnout limit sends none.

Headgate dwell timing
Holding a gate card's dwell control for one second commits the stroke with progress reading 0 to 100 in step with the time held, and releasing earlier, losing focus, the page becoming hidden or the card being handed over resets it to 0 and sends nothing.

Space-held dwell
Holding Space on the focused dwell control works exactly like a pointer hold, keyboard auto-repeat neither restarts nor speeds the dwell, and releasing Space early cancels it.

Touch long-press dwell
On a 375-wide touch screen a long press on the dwell control runs the dwell without opening the browser's press menu, selecting text or panning the page.

Delivered only after the store confirms
A committed stroke shows that it is waiting for the store and moves no flow or delivered figure until the object store confirms its stroke record, as qualified in Business rules.

Spent card never strokes twice
A gate card that is waiting for the store or spent refuses every further stroke with 409, and once spent it shows its stroke record in place of a dwell control.

Flow numeral rises on confirmation
On confirmation the card's channel flow figure counts from the old to the new ML/day over 0.6 seconds and the delivered figure runs up to its new value, and both show their final values at once under reduced motion.

Stroke announcements
The Gate dwell status live region announces early release, sent, stored, handover, store-outage and window-not-open results with the copy in Feedback states.

Field stroke journey
A channel operator opens `/field`, holds the dwell on a start card until the stroke is stored, and sees the order running, the channel flow raised and a new finish card in their list.

Holder succession
Removing an open gate card's holder hands it to the order's standby or else the window's rostered operator as Business rules orders it, and the removed operator is then refused with 409 `not_holder`.

Mid-flow handover journey
A dispatcher removes the holder of a running order's finish card and the successor finishes the delivery with one stroke, with no second start stroke and the delivered total counting the order once.

Order state machine
Orders move only along the transitions in Business rules, and every other move answers 409 `illegal_transition` without changing the order, window or allocation.

Dispatcher close and reopen
A dispatcher closes a requested, scheduled or running order and reopens one closed while running, with the volume, allocation, turnout and window checks in Business rules.

Lapse at the window's close
From the first read at or after a window's closing instant, its requested and scheduled orders read closed with `conflict` `lapsed`, with their volume, allocation and start cards released, while running orders stay running.

Honest board order actions
While Schedule, Close, Reopen or Ration is pending on the board's Orders panel the rows and counters keep the server's figures, and after the reply they show the server's returned or re-read figures, never guessed ones, as Feedback states sets.

Publish a pro-rated restriction
`POST /api/windows/<window id>/restrictions` sets one cap from its effective minute, pro-rates the window's cap volume by the rule in Business rules, and moves scheduled orders that no longer fit back to requested in the published order.

Restriction notices
Each publish sends one restriction notice to every grower with a scheduled, running or just-moved order in the window, as Services defines, and when the mail service is down the notices queue and go out later.

Restrictions update open screens in place
Within 5 seconds of a publish, a grower's open order form, the search suggestions, the board cells and the remaining and delivered counters show the new cap and remaining volume without a reload, with the announcement in Feedback states.

Restriction shortcut
Pressing R anywhere on the board outside a text field opens the Publish restriction dialog for the selected window.

Restriction publish journey
A dispatcher selects a window, publishes a restriction from the dialog and lands on `/restrictions/<restriction id>`, which shows the cap, the moved orders and the published announcement and shows the same view on reload.

Daylight-saving-true windows
A dispatcher-created window's hours are elapsed hours and its label shows each instant at the district offset in force, so windows across the April and October changes run 25 or 23 hours with the matching cap volume, and an instant in April's repeated hour carries AEDT or AEST in its label.

Capacity table revisions
Each save of a channel's capacity table on its current revision creates the next revision, and caps whose cap volume would fall below what a window has already committed are refused with 422.

Conflicting saves settle to the lower cap
A save based on an older revision stores a new revision in which every submitted cell is the lower of the current and submitted caps, and answers 409 `revision_conflict` with both sets.

Conflict dialog keeps typed numbers
After a conflicting save, the Capacity table conflict dialog shows the dispatcher's typed numbers beside the settled caps, and the typed numbers stay on screen after the dialog closes.

Typed caps survive live refresh
While a dispatcher edits the capacity table, live refreshes update clean cells, remaining figures and the revision list but never typed cells, the save's base revision or an open conflict dialog, as Interactions sets.

Restore an earlier revision
Restoring a revision creates a new revision with that revision's caps while every order and restriction keeps its window, status and volume, and a restore that would fall below committed volume is refused with 409.

Capacity table journey
Two dispatchers edit the same table, the second sees the conflict dialog with the settled caps, and an earlier revision is then restored from the revision list with the new revision announced in Capacity status.

Board layout at published viewports
The channel board shows three panes at 1280x800, a collapsed rail with a modal detail sheet at 768x1024, and an off-canvas channel drawer with one window per row at 375x812, as Screens and layout describes.

Collapsed means unavailable
A collapsed channel rail, a closed channel drawer, a closed detail sheet and a closed section expander are hidden, out of the Tab order and absent from the accessibility tree at every published viewport.

Board state in the address bar
The board's channel filter, selected window and active tab live in the address as published, so back, forward, reload and pasted links restore the same board.

Live search suggestions
Typing two or more characters into the search box lists up to 8 suggestions for turnouts, growers, channels and operators within the caller's reach, each with the label, detail and link Business rules publishes for its kind and the caller's role, and the list updates as the user types.

Pack preview and signed submission
The records clerk previews a pack for a period, signs it, and submits exactly the previewed text, and the submission is refused with 409 `pack_stale` if the records changed since the preview.

Pack periods in district dates
A pack period and a totals date range cover exactly the windows whose opening falls on those Australia/Sydney dates, with district-zone labels including the repeated-hour zone marks, also across a daylight-saving change.

Stored and mailed together
A submitted pack is stored in the object store and then mailed once to the regulator, is never mailed without its stored object, and is visible to the reviewer only after both, as qualified in Business rules.

Pack submission journey
The clerk previews, signs and submits a pack, lands on `/packs/<pack id>`, and hears the completion announcement in Pack status once the pack is stored and mailed.

Stalled pack shows outage copy
While the object store or the mail service is down, a pack stalls at building or stored and its page shows the matching outage copy verbatim.

Stalled work resumes by itself
A stalled pack, a stroke waiting for the store and queued notices finish within 30 seconds of the missing service answering again, with nobody restarting anything.

Withdraw a stalled pack
The clerk withdraws a pack that is not yet mailed, which deletes any stored object and guarantees no mail is ever sent for it.

Erase a contractor
`DELETE /api/contractors/<operator code>` by the records clerk removes the contractor's name, phone and email from every stored record and from search, while their orders, strokes and cards keep the operator code.

Erasure ends access at once
After a contractor is erased, the very next request on any of their sessions answers 401 `not_signed_in`, their open field view goes to `/sign-in` within 5 seconds, and their old credentials answer 401 `bad_credentials`.

Copies carry operator codes only
Notices, stroke records and regulator packs identify every gate worker by operator code only, never by name or phone.

Contractor erasure journey
The clerk erases a departed contractor from `/contractors`, any open card they held moves by the holder succession rule, and searching their name afterwards finds nothing.

Reviewer is read-only
The state regulator reviewer reads mailed packs, capacity tables and channel totals, and every write endpoint answers 403 `forbidden` for them.

Pack download byte for byte
Downloading a mailed pack returns exactly the bytes the clerk submitted, identical to the stored object and to the mailed attachment, and the SHA-256 shown on the pack page and in the pack mail is the hash of those bytes.

Live review page
The reviewer's open Review page updates its totals and lists each newly mailed pack within 5 seconds without a reload, announces it in Review status, and never shows an unmailed or withdrawn pack.

One source for every total
The board, the order form, the grower's allocation and the reviewer's channel totals show values derived from the same stored window and allocation figures, and they agree after every order, cancel, close, reopen, lapse, restriction, ration, save, restore and stroke.

Proportional ration
`POST /api/windows/<window id>/ration` schedules the window's candidate requested orders at shares of its remaining ML in proportion to each demand capped by the turnout's max volume and the grower's allocation, rounded down to 0.001 ML with leftover thousandths by largest remainder so the shares sum exactly to the remaining ML, as Business rules sets.

Ration never overfills
A ration is judged in the same single step as placements, schedules and restriction publishes, so a ration racing them never leaves committed volume above cap volume or debits an allocation twice, and every reply is a published status.

Ration notices
Each grower with at least one ration candidate gets exactly one ration notice with the published line for each candidate and operator codes only, queued while the mail service is down as Services describes.

Ration journey
A dispatcher opens Ration window on the board's Orders panel, confirms in the Ration dialog, and sees Board status announce the result while the rows show the shares and asked volumes from the server's reply.

Ended session keeps the order draft
A grower whose session ends while on the order form goes to sign-in with a return path and, after signing in again as the same grower, finds every field as they left it with the published notice and nothing placed.

Replies belong to the caller
However many growers' requests are in flight at once, every order reply, allocation figure and 422 allocation message belongs to the calling grower, and each conflict notice goes to the grower whose order lost.

Handovers reach open field views
Within 5 seconds of a handover the successor's open field view shows the card and the removed holder's view drops it, each announced in Gate dwell status, a dwell in progress on the moved card is cancelled with nothing sent, and a remove-holder racing a stroke has exactly one winner.

Board follows the server's window close
Within 5 seconds of a window's closing instant the open board shows its lapsed rows with the lapsed status label and without Schedule or Reopen, keeps running rows Running with Close, and shows the restored remaining ML, whatever the device clock says.

Restriction dialog survives its timers
Reopening the Publish restriction dialog during its exit transition leaves it open, and no live repaint clears its typed values, its field errors or the Board status error copy until the next user action.

Capacity table at published viewports
The capacity table sits beside its revision list at 1280x800, above it at 768x1024 and as one stacked block per window at 375x812, with the conflict dialog full-screen on a phone, as Screens and layout describes.

Review period in the address
The reviewer's chosen totals period lives in the Review page address, so Show totals, back, forward, reload and pasted links restore the period inputs and the Channel totals table.

Turnout outlet limit
Each turnout's outlet limit caps an order's volume in a window at the turnout's max volume, and the quote and `POST /api/orders` refuse a larger volume with the 422 in API, checked after the range and before the allocation.

Honest Place order
While Place order is pending the Allocation counter and Window remaining keep the server's figures and Place order is disabled, and after `window_full` or the allocation error they show the 409 `remaining_ml` and a re-read allocation, as Feedback states sets.

Grower order views follow the server
A grower's open order page and home order list show every server change to their orders within 5 seconds without a reload, including the lapse at the window's close under a wrong device clock, announced in Order status with the copy in Feedback states.

Lapse notice exactly once
Each grower with an order that lapsed in a window gets exactly one lapse notice created in the same step as the lapse, however many reads judge it at once, queued while the mail service is down as Services describes.

Keyboard-complete contractor erasure
The Erase contractor dialog keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside it, Escape returns focus to its Erase button, and after erasure that button stays focused and disabled and sends nothing when pressed.

Review page at published viewports
The Review page puts Channel totals beside Mailed packs at 1280x800, above it at 768x1024 and as one stacked block per window at 375x812 with table semantics kept, as Screens and layout describes.

Ration dialog survives its timers
Reopening the Ration dialog during its exit transition leaves it open, live refreshes update its figures without closing it or moving focus, and no live repaint re-enables a pending ration or clears the Board status ration result until the next user action.
`/app/run.json` is valid JSON with exactly the string keys `_schema` (value `run-manifest-v1`), `install`, `build` and `serve`.
`/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` names every shipped package and every bundled font with its licence. Shipped packages are the production dependency tree reported by `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`.
Every shipped package (as defined in IF-02) and every bundled font is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or OFL-1.1.
The app stores data only in the provided Postgres database and MinIO bucket: no SQLite, Redis, embedded database or data files on disk.
`/app/package-lock.json` is committed, and `install` uses it.
The provided service configuration (the dev compose files and their seeded credentials) is left unchanged.
The served app makes no network requests to hosts other than its own origin and the three provided services.
